brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE JANUARY, 1953

“ My own mother is 88 and suffers from arthritis, which is alleviated by her infra-red lamp; a switch at her bedside illuminates her clock to enable her to see how the tedious hours are passing; if the nights are chilly, there is a switch for the electric blanket; an electric kettle gives her a reviving cup of tea; and a switch controls the wireless set at the other end of the house, giving her a programme on her bedroom loudspeaker. On the arm of her chair are three switches which enable her, with a touch of the hand, to turn on and off her standard lamp, radio, and the warming footpad, which is such a comfort to the poor circulation of age.”

What a contrast!

These blessings are no longer the prerogative of the rich, and transcend anything even the rich could secure 50 years ago.

A few weeks ago I visited the home of one of our so-called "problem" families. WE all know the two forms of
frustration in furnishing —

brief_context: Mentioned as introducing fire-prevention in history of fire-fighting.
brief_extract: Smith, Chief Fire Officer, spoke on "The History of the Fire Service," tracing the history of organised fire-fighting from early China, through Roman times, to the days of the Crusaders, who had to defend their wooden ships on the way to the Holy Land. Later King Alfred introduced fire-prevention in the daub and wattle houses of the time, and William the Conqueror ordered the curfew, corruption of "Couvre-feu." Fire insurance came after the "Fire of London," each company's fire brigade attending fires only at premises bearing their firemark outside. Big changes came in 1935-6, when a Royal Commission was set up.

brief_context: Chairman of the Committee of Enquiry on Air Pollution.
article_title: SMOKE POLLUTION - The Housewife's Point of View
brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE OCTOBER, 1953

SMOKE POLLUTION

The Housewife's Point of View

THE housewife has long been aware of the evils of atmospheric pollution, and smoke abatement has been one of the aims of the Electrical Association for Women since its inception in 1924. Today the whole national conscience has been aroused by the disastrous fog of December 1952, and has welcomed the Committee of Enquiry on Air Pollution set up under the Chairmanship of Sir Hugh Beaver, with the following terms of reference:

" To examine the nature, cause, and effects of air pollution, and the efficacy of present preventive measures; to con- sider what further preventive measures are practicable; and to make recommenda- tions."

While it is perhaps easier to measure the quantity and effect of air pollution from the industrial stand-point, the housewife has a very special interest in the matter for it is directly related to her housekeeping and to the health of her family. The Electrical Association for Women is there- fore preparing a survey to gain an indication of the effect of air pollution on household running and household budgets, and invites the assistance of any interested housewives.
